event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: TSN’s 10-K frames COVID-19 as a still-present, multi-faceted threat that has already produced concrete operational, financial and legal impacts while remaining highly uncertain going forward.  Because the filing date (14-Nov-2022) is less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time-Decay Principle allows elevated severity scores.  The disclosure set is mostly specific and backward-looking—detailing actual plant slowdowns, higher health-safety spending, litigation and supply-chain cost spikes—but it also projects further volatility in labour availability, consumer demand and logistics.  Few hard dollar figures are supplied, so the risk evidence stops short of the maximum 10/10 threshold, yet the breadth of functions affected (production, costs, demand, legal) and the acknowledgement of materiality justify upper-mid scores.  Mitigations (e.g., monitoring, vaccinations) are mentioned but not shown to neutralise the risk.  Overall, COVID-19 remains a direct, recent and significant risk driver for TSN, warranting strong—but not maximal—snippet scores in the 5-8 range.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated responses has had, and may to continue to have, an adverse impact on our business and operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to adverse business impact (direct causation).
States both historical and future impact (‘has had, and may continue’).
Generic—no quantitative detail or business line specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct admission of past and future harm, but generic wording and no numbers keep the score at 5/10.

evidence_list.snippet: During the pandemic, we experienced slowdowns at certain of our production facilities, primarily due to a decrease in our available workforce, and we anticipate that we may in the future experience additional volatility in our ability to operate our facilities at full utilization rates, depending on a number of factors including team member absenteeism, labor shortages and other workforce disruptions.

components.reason: Reports realised operational disruption (facility slowdowns).
Details the causal mechanism (workforce decrease, absenteeism).
Projects future volatility, extending risk horizon.
No quantified magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, realised disruption and clear forward-looking risk yield a high score of 7/10 despite lack of dollar amounts.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced, and expect to continue to experience, an increase in operating costs in connection with higher costs associated with ensuring the continued health and safety of team members, including team member costs associated with worker health and availability such as COVID-19 testing and vaccinations.

components.reason: Identifies concrete financial impact (higher operating costs).
Specifies cost drivers (testing, vaccinations, health measures).
States expectation of continued cost pressure.
No numeric quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear cost impact and persistence justify 6/10; absence of figures prevents a higher score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, certain of our team members who claim to have tested positive for COVID-19, or their family members, have filed lawsuits seeking compensatory and punitive damages for wrongful death and personal injury claims in several states, and additional team members or family members of team members may assert similar claims as the COVID-19 pandemic continues.

components.reason: Reveals actual litigation already filed (realised legal exposure).
Potential for additional claims expands future liability scope.
Mentions compensatory and punitive damages, implying materiality.
No estimate of financial magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Existing lawsuits plus risk of more give moderate-high severity; lack of dollar detail caps score at 5/10.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also experienced, and expect to continue to experience, disruption and volatility in our supply chain, which has resulted, and may continue to result, in increased costs for certain raw materials, packaging materials and transportation costs.

components.reason: Admits realised supply-chain disruption affecting costs.
Covers multiple cost categories (raw materials, packaging, transportation).
Forecasts ongoing impact.
No numeric sizing.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad cost impacts across the chain but unquantified, yielding 5/10.

evidence_list.snippet: The spread of COVID-19 and other related supply chain issues have also disrupted and may continue to disrupt logistics necessary to import, export and deliver products to us and our customers.

components.reason: Highlights logistics disruption impacting both inbound and outbound flows.
States risk is ongoing (‘may continue’).
No financial or operational magnitude provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific to logistics but relatively generic and unquantified, so mid-low score of 3/10.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of school and in-restaurant dining shutdowns during the COVID-19 pandemic, each of our segments previously experienced a shift in demand from foodservice to retail.

components.reason: Describes concrete change in demand patterns across all segments.
Links change directly to pandemic shutdowns.
Refers to past experience; no forward quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Historic demand shock noted but no projection or dollar impact; score 3/10.

evidence_list.snippet: While each of our segments has subsequently experienced varying levels of foodservice recovery, the long-term impact of COVID-19 remains uncertain and will depend on a number of future developments, which are uncertain and cannot be predicted at this time.

components.reason: Acknowledges lingering uncertainty regarding long-term demand effects.
Highlights inability to predict, increasing risk volatility.
No direct impact or figures supplied.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises uncertainty but little specificity; modest 2/10.

evidence_list.snippet: If a significant percentage of our workforce is unable to work, including because of illness, this could have an adverse effect on our operations and results of operations.

components.reason: Connects workforce illness to adverse operational and financial impact.
Highlights potential scale (‘significant percentage’).
Hypothetical—impact not yet quantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potentially severe labour risk but framed hypothetically, so 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: The most significant challenge we face is the availability of team members to operate our production facilities as our production facilities continue to experience varying levels of absenteeism.

components.reason: Labels labour availability as the company’s ‘most significant challenge’.
Indicates ongoing absenteeism affecting production capacity.
No numeric disclosure of impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong wording on critical labour risk, but lack of data keeps score at 5/10.
